summary: Nintendo's detective visual novel duology, with classic Famicom Disk System originals, Japanese Virtual Console reissues, and modern Nintendo Switch remakes.

entries.title: Famicom Detective Club: The Girl Who Stands Behind
entries.definitive_edition: Famicom Detective Club: The Girl Who Stands Behind (Nintendo Switch, 2021)

emulation.notes: Use the official Switch release for the main run. Classic FDS/GBA/Virtual Console versions are only needed for historical comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official Switch remake presentation, docked HD capture

primary.version: 2021 MAGES remake, standalone or bundled with the other Famicom Detective Club remake
primary.why: The original Famicom Detective Club case and the 2021 Nintendo Switch remake both exist; the Switch release is modernized with updated visuals, fully voiced cutscenes, and English on-screen text. The Switch remake is therefore the highest-fidelity and most accessible complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the official Nintendo Switch release, standalone or from the two-game bundle. Use docked output for clean capture, English on-screen text, and Japanese voiceover; keep Famicom/GBA/Virtual Console versions only for historical comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Original two-disk Famicom Disk System presentation; historically authoritative but 8-bit, Japanese-only, and lower fidelity than later remakes.
all_releases.reason: skip: the 1989 NES/Famicom Disk System release exists, but the Switch remake covers the same case with modern presentation and official English text.

all_releases.fidelity: Earlier enhanced remake with improved graphics and sound over Famicom and an added memo feature, but still Japan-only and below the Switch remake's visual/voice scope.
all_releases.reason: skip: worth archival comparison because it is a distinct official remake, but no exclusive story route is sourced and the 2021 Switch remake is the better primary for fidelity and localization.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable reissue of the classic-era game; useful for preservation, but limited by GBA resolution and Japanese-only availability.
all_releases.reason: skip: a GBA release exists, but it does not beat the Switch remake for fidelity or localization and no exclusive content exists.

all_releases.fidelity: Official emulated reissue of the classic version on Wii; preserves the older presentation rather than remaking it.
all_releases.reason: skip: a Wii version exists, but the release is a Virtual Console path to the classic game and has no exclusive content over Switch.

all_releases.fidelity: Official handheld Virtual Console reissue; convenient but limited by 3DS display resolution and classic assets.
all_releases.reason: skip: a Nintendo 3DS version exists, but it is not the highest-fidelity route and no exclusive case content exists.

all_releases.fidelity: Official console Virtual Console reissue of the classic version; cleaner capture than original hardware but still the older release.
all_releases.reason: skip: a Wii U version exists, but the Switch remake is the fidelity and localization pick and no exclusive content exists here.

all_releases.fidelity: Modern remake with updated visuals, animation, Japanese voice acting, and official English on-screen text.
all_releases.reason: primary: best fidelity and most accessible complete playthrough; it traces to the 1989 original, and the Switch release is localized and modernized.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No story, mission, or ending content is missing from the Switch remake; older releases are preservation routes rather than required secondary playthroughs.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Switch release uses Japanese voiceover with English on-screen text and modernizes presentation while retaining menu-driven investigation structure. Older Famicom, GBA, and Virtual Console releases remain useful only for historical comparison.
